title: 師傅坐了三十年的那張歪椅子
description: 學徒做壞的第一張椅子,師傅為什麼坐了三十年?一個關於起步的小故事。
style: soft watercolor storybook illustration, warm muted earth tones, gentle golden light, hand-painted texture, cinematic wide composition, no text, no letters, no watermark

characters.MASTER: an elderly Taiwanese carpenter with short grey hair, thin round glasses and a faded indigo apron
characters.BOY: a skinny sixteen-year-old Taiwanese apprentice boy with messy black hair and a plain white shirt
characters.MAN: a middle-aged Taiwanese carpenter with short black hair touched with grey, wearing a faded indigo apron

scenes.narration: 阿樹十六歲那年,做出了人生第一張椅子。四隻腳,有一隻短了半公分。
scenes.image: BOY kneeling on the floor of a small old woodshop, staring at a simple wooden chair that leans slightly to one side, wood shavings on the floor

scenes.narration: 他紅著臉,想趁師傅沒看到,把它劈了當柴燒。
scenes.image: BOY nervously carrying the crooked wooden chair toward a firewood pile behind the woodshop at dusk, looking over his shoulder

scenes.narration: 師傅卻把椅子接了過去,放在店門口,坐了下來。椅子晃了一下,師傅什麼也沒說。
scenes.image: MASTER sitting calmly on the slightly crooked wooden chair at the entrance of a small woodshop on an old street, BOY watching from inside the doorway

scenes.narration: 從那天起,師傅每天都坐那張椅子。客人笑它歪,阿樹每看一次,就難受一次。
scenes.image: MASTER sitting on the crooked chair outside the woodshop drinking tea while two passing customers smile and point at the chair, BOY in the background looking down

scenes.narration: 於是他拼命練。十年後,他做的椅子,整條街都搶著訂。可是門口那張歪椅子,師傅始終不肯換。
scenes.image: MAN in his late twenties working with intense focus at a workbench surrounded by many beautifully finished wooden chairs, warm lamp light, the old crooked chair visible by the open door

scenes.narration: 三十年後,師傅要退休了。阿樹終於忍不住問:您為什麼,偏偏要坐我做得最差的那一張?
scenes.image: MAN standing beside MASTER who is very old now with white hair, both next to the worn crooked chair at the woodshop entrance, late afternoon light

scenes.narration: 師傅摸著椅背笑了:這張椅子我坐了三十年,它從來沒有垮過。歪,不代表不能用。
scenes.image: close view of the very old MASTER with white hair smiling gently, his wrinkled hand resting on the worn backrest of the crooked wooden chair

scenes.narration: 而且每次看到它,我就想起來,再厲害的師傅,都是從歪的那一張開始的。
scenes.image: the old crooked wooden chair alone in a beam of golden sunlight at the woodshop entrance, a row of perfect chairs softly blurred in the background

scenes.narration: 如果你現在做的東西還很歪,別急著把它燒掉。那是你的第一張椅子。
scenes.image: MAN now the shop owner placing the old crooked chair at the entrance in morning light while a new young apprentice watches from the workbench
